title: TOPIX gets more selective: liquidity and free float now decide who keeps full benchmark weight

claims.text: JPX Market Innovation & Research announced the first periodic review and initial selection for the next-generation TOPIX on October 7, 2026.

JPX's October 7 first selection adds 35 stocks (23 Standard-market and 12 Growth-market listings); 683 existing constituents enter transitional weighting reductions. The projected July 2028 total of 986 constituents is conditional because the October 2027 reassessment can allow some transitional names to remain.
claims.basis: JPX October 7 selection notice and Reuters' enumeration of the released JPX lists; the 986 total is not a guaranteed final count.

claims.text: Existing TOPIX constituents must have an annual traded value ratio of at least 0.14 and fall within the top 97% of cumulative free-float-adjusted market capitalization to meet continuation criteria; new additions face stricter 0.20 and top-96% thresholds.
claims.basis: JPX next-generation TOPIX methodology and FAQ.

claims.text: Issues not selected at the first periodic review enter an eight-stage quarterly weighting reduction, with a re-evaluation in October 2027 that can stop the reduction for issues that regain the continuation criteria.

Benchmark membership is becoming more explicitly tied to investability rather than simply being listed in a particular TSE segment, increasing the incentive for smaller companies to improve liquidity and genuinely tradable free float.
claims.basis: Inference from JPX's liquidity-based cross-market selection rules.

content.history: TOPIX historically had a strong link to TSE market-segment membership. The next-generation framework opens selection across Prime, Standard and Growth while applying annual liquidity and free-float-adjusted market-cap tests.

takeaways: TOPIX selection now explicitly emphasizes trading liquidity and free-float-adjusted market capitalization.
Existing constituents and new entrants face different thresholds.
Non-selected constituents are phased down over eight quarterly steps rather than removed at once.
For passive investors, this is a benchmark-methodology change, not evidence that every deleted company is fundamentally weak.

content.connection: The reform connects index construction with Japan's broader push toward more investable public markets and stronger incentives for companies to improve market liquidity and investor accessibility.
watch_next: The October 30, 2026 start of the first transition step and TOPIX Next-tier.

evidence_for: JPX has published the first periodic-review and initial-selection results.
The continuation and inclusion thresholds are explicitly defined by JPX.
JPX has scheduled eight quarterly weighting reductions for non-selected constituents.
Selection now covers domestic common shares across Prime, Standard and Growth subject to the methodology.
The first actual selection has 35 new additions and 683 transitional constituents; the projected 986 constituents in July 2028 remains conditional on reassessment.
implications: Broad TOPIX funds will gradually track a more liquidity-screened investable universe.
Companies near the thresholds have a stronger benchmark-related incentive to improve tradable free float and market liquidity.
Index deletion or reduced weight should not be treated by itself as a verdict on business quality.

30_sec: TOPIX is entering its next-generation selection regime.
First selection: 35 new additions, 683 existing names under phased reductions; 986 projected for July 2028 is not final.
Liquidity and free float now explicitly determine continuation and new inclusion.
Non-selected names are phased down over eight quarterly steps.
The transition runs with a 2027 re-evaluation and a second periodic review in 2028.
reading_levels.2_min: TOPIX is becoming more selective. JPX announced the first periodic review and initial selection on October 7, 2026. Existing constituents need an annual traded value ratio of at least 0.14 and must sit within the top 97% of cumulative free-float-adjusted market capitalization among qualifying issues; new additions face stricter thresholds. Companies that do not qualify are not removed overnight: their weights are reduced in eight quarterly stages, with a re-evaluation in October 2027. Ang signal: benchmark representation is becoming more explicitly tied to actual investability. For ordinary TOPIX-fund investors, this is mainly a gradual methodology change—not a reason to trade individual additions or deletions. JPX's first actual list adds 35 names (23 Standard, 12 Growth) and puts 683 existing names under phased weighting reductions. The 986-constituent July 2028 projection is conditional, dahil puwedeng makabalik ang ilang names sa 2027 reassessment.

evidence_against: The phased transition reduces the immediate market impact.
Index selection is a methodology decision and does not directly measure company fundamentals or future returns.
Companies under transitional measures can regain continuation eligibility at the October 2027 re-evaluation.
content.what_would_change_mind: The structural thesis would weaken if JPX materially postpones or reverses the published transition, abandons the liquidity/free-float criteria, or stops the scheduled weighting reductions.
content.alternative_explanation: Some apparent pressure on smaller companies may reflect ordinary market-cap and trading changes rather than corporate actions taken specifically to preserve TOPIX representation.

summary: JPX's first next-generation TOPIX selection adds 35 stocks and places 683 existing constituents under eight quarterly weighting reductions. The projected 986 constituents by July 2028 is conditional on the October 2027 re-evaluation. Liquidity and free float, rather than market segment alone, increasingly determine benchmark representation.
why_it_matters: TOPIX is a core benchmark for Japanese equities. Its transition changes which listed companies receive full benchmark representation and creates stronger incentives around liquidity and investable free float.
